in_arabic.name: تحية
in_arabic.meaning: تحية تعارف و احترام کے لئے استعمال ہونے والا اسم
in_arabic.long_meaning: تحية اسم ہے جو تعارف و احترام کے لئے استعمال ہوتا ہے، اور اس کا مطلب ہے 'حیات' یا 'زندگی' دینے والا۔ یہ نام اہل تشیع میں شہادت کے لئے استعمال ہوتا ہے، خاص طور پر حضرت فاطمہ زہرا (س) کے لئے۔

in_urdu.name: تحیہ
in_urdu.meaning: تحیہ سلامتی اور احترام کے لیے استعمال ہونے والا نام
in_urdu.long_meaning: تحیہ ایک ایسا نام ہے جو سلامتی اور احترام کے لیے استعمال ہوتا ہے۔ اس کا مطلب ہے 'حیات' یا 'زندگی' دینے والا، اور یہ اہل تشیع میں شہادت کے لیے استعمال ہوتا ہے، خاص طور پر حضرت فاطمہ زہرا (س) کے لیے۔

in_hindi.name: तहिया
in_hindi.meaning: तहिया शांति और सम्मान के लिए उपयोग होने वाला नाम
in_hindi.long_meaning: तहिया एक ऐसा नाम है जो शांति और सम्मान के लिए उपयोग होता है। इसका अर्थ है 'जीवन' या 'जीवंत' देने वाला, और यह शियाओं में शहादत के लिए उपयोग होता है, विशेष रूप से हज़रत फातिमा ज़हरा (स) के लिए।

in_pashto.name: تحیہ
in_pashto.meaning: تحیہ د ژوند او درننګۍ لپاره کارول شوی نوم
in_pashto.long_meaning: تحیہ هغه نوم دی چی د ژوند او درننګۍ لپاره کارول کیږی. دغه نوم د شیعه ګانو په مذهب کی د شہادت لپاره کارول کیږی، په ځانګړی ډول د حضرت فاطمہ زہرا (س) لپاره.

in_english.name: Tahiyya
in_english.meaning: Tahiyya means 'one who gives life' or 'bringer of life'
in_english.long_meaning: Tahiyya is a name that originates from Arabic roots, meaning 'one who gives life' or 'bringer of life'. It is used in Shia tradition to signify martyrdom, particularly in reference to Lady Fatimah Zahra (peace be upon her). The name carries deep spiritual significance, symbolizing the essence of life and vitality.

data.cultural_impact: The phrase "Tahiyyat ul-Masjid" (Arabic: تهية المسجد) is a common greeting used among Muslims while entering a mosque. The term "Tahiyyat" is the Arabic word for "greetings" or "salutations," and the phrase is used to convey respect and love for the sacred place of worship. This custom embodies the collective ethos of Islamic culture, which values respect, humility, and community, particularly while entering a sacred place.
data.spiritual_significance: Tahiyyat is a reminder of our faith and love for Allah, as we offer praise and gratitude through the act of greeting each other and acknowledging the sanctity of a place of worship. By utilizing the phrase "Tahiyyat ul-Masjid," Muslims consciously express reverence towards their creator and reinforce the spiritual bond within the community, fostering a deeper connection with Allah and each other.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Tahiyya bint Khalid ibn al-Asad al-Tamimi was a prominent female companion of the Prophet Muhammad. The name Tahiyya carried significant weight in that era.
historical_references.context: Tahiyya was a noblewoman from the Banu Tamim tribe and was known for her generosity and hospitality towards the Prophet Muhammad and his companions. She was also a skilled poetess and is said to have composed verses in praise of the Prophet.
